Don’t start with the hardest part of your business.

Start with the boring thing that happens all day.

Think about clearing out your house.

You don’t start with the garage.

The garage takes a month.

You start with the kitchen drawer you open every single day.

Ten minutes, and you feel it straight away.

Your business works the same way.

The big, messy thing is tempting.

“Let’s fix the whole booking system.”
“Let’s put AI on everything.”
“Let’s redo how we handle complaints.”

It takes months.

You can’t tell if it worked.

And by then, nobody remembers how it was before.

Now look at the boring things instead.

The booking confirmation you send by hand.
The “what time do you open?” message you answer ten times a day.
The reminder text someone forgets on busy days.

Nobody gets excited about these.

But they happen all day.

So when you fix one, you see the difference within a week.
Fewer missed texts.
Fewer no-shows.
Fewer interruptions.

And that’s when you know it’s worth doing the next one.

Boring and frequent beats big and complicated.

Every time.
